core_obligations: Prove the lifting statement for morphisms of Deligne systems from the corepresentation description (proof lines 8144-8152).
Construct the Deligne system by powers of an ideal applied to a bounded complex representing a lift of K (proof lines 8154-8166).
Derive uniqueness of the pro-object from the previous two parts (proof lines 8168-8170).
proof_roadmap: Part (2) by the ideal power construction (proof lines 8154-8166).
difficulty_reason: For an open immersion j : U -> X of Noetherian schemes, the lemma asserts three things: given Deligne systems (K_n), (L_n) with constant values K and L on U, every morphism alpha : K -> L of D(O_U) lifts uniquely to a morphism of pro-systems (K_n) -> (L_n) in D^b_Coh(O_X); every K in D^b_Coh(O_U) admits a Deligne system whose restriction to U is constant with value K; and that pro-object is unique up to unique isomorphism (statement lines 8102-8142). Part (1) is immediate from Lemma labelled lemma-lift-map and the description of morphisms of pro-systems as morphisms of the functors they corepresent in Categories, Remark labelled categories-remark-pro-category-copresheaves (proof lines 8144-8152). For (2) the proof chooses K' in D^b_Coh(O_X) restricting to K by Derived Categories of Schemes, Lemma labelled perfect-lemma-lift-coherent, represents it by a bounded complex F^bullet of coherent modules by Derived Categories of Schemes, Proposition labelled perfect-proposition-DCoh, chooses a quasi-coherent ideal I with vanishing locus X minus U, and sets K_n to be the object represented by I^n F^bullet as in the introduction to the section (proof lines 8154-8166). Part (3) then follows from (1) and (2) (proof lines 8168-8170). Realising the lift as the system of powers of an ideal and deducing uniqueness from the universal property of pro-systems is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
